# GitHub Copilot Repository Instructions

This project is a collection of educational resources for frontend development, with an emphasis on JavaScript concepts, utilities, data structures, algorithms, and machine-coding examples.

## Project Conventions

- Files are organized in a hierarchical folder structure by topic category
- All file names use snake_case naming convention
- Markdown files include emojis in headings to improve navigation and readability
- Code examples should be practical, well-commented, and follow modern JavaScript conventions

## Content Structure

Each educational resource should follow this general structure:
1. Title with emoji and clear description
2. Introduction to the concept
3. Core concepts and technical details
4. Multiple practical use cases with code examples
5. Limitations or considerations
6. Summary/key takeaways
7. Final thoughts on broader implications

## Coding Style

- Use modern ES6+ JavaScript syntax
- Prefer arrow functions for callbacks
- Use `const` by default, `let` when necessary, and avoid `var`
- Include TypeScript types where applicable
- Comments should be concise and explain "why" rather than "what"
- Always include error handling in examples

## Project Organization

- `/dsa` - Data structures and algorithms
- `/general` - General frontend concepts
- `/js` - JavaScript-specific topics
  - `/general-concepts` - Core JavaScript concepts
  - `/polyfills` - Implementations of standard methods
  - `/promises` - Promise-related patterns
  - `/utils` - Utility functions
- `/machine-coding` - Practical implementation examples
- `/ai` - AI and LLM integration resources

When providing suggestions or answering questions, reference existing files as a guide for maintaining consistency in style and structure.
